title: Code Reviewer workflow, version 1
description: A workflow is a JSON document (#833, agent workflows, app/src/workflows/, docs/workflows.md): one or more triggers and a list of steps that run in order. Five kinds of node: the trigger, the agent step, the action, the control nodes `if` and `loop`, and (reserved) the workflow as a step. Nodes talk to each other only through values: a text may hold `{{step.field}}` references to what an earlier step yielded. The schema states the form, closed everywhere: a key it does not name is refused. What it cannot state is checked by the validator, which also gives every problem a JSON pointer, a stable code, the cause and the names that were available: that every reference points at a step that ran before on every path, the types of the values that flow, the ids, limits, and that profiles and environments exist. A workflow has several triggers (#916), each with pre-steps of its own; when one fires, its pre-steps run and then the shared steps, so the shared steps read only what every trigger yields. A run works on ONE repository: the one of its trigger (the ticket's: `trigger.ticket.repo` of a label trigger and of a manual or api trigger with a `ticket` input, the input `repo` of a manual one), so a node names none. The single `trigger` of format 1 before #916 is still read, as a list of one trigger without pre-steps; `github.issueLabeled` is read as `ticket.labeled`. The inputs that decide a TARGET (the issue, the branches, the labels, the environment) take a literal or one whole reference to a value the platform or the caller vouches for (the issue or ticket number, the default branch, an input of a manual trigger, the branch of an agent step), never a value an agent reported and never the title, body or labels of the issue, which whoever opened it wrote: the validator holds them to it (`target_from_untrusted_value`). A reader ignores nothing: unknown fields are errors. `forEach`, `approval` and `workflow` are named here so a document can use them later; version 1 refuses them (code `kind_not_supported`). Written by the app (src/workflows/); the version is in the path and in `version`.

trigger.description: The single trigger of format 1 before #916, read as a list of one trigger without pre-steps.

triggers.description: The triggers that start the workflow, one to ten, each with pre-steps of its own. A workflow has `triggers` or the single `trigger` of the older form, not both.

budgetUsd.description: What the workflow may spend in USD over all its steps; 20 when left out, and not above the operator's maximum (the validator).

turnTimeLimitMinutes.description: How long one agent turn of the workflow may run, in whole minutes (#918): 15 to 60, 60 when left out (the Dispatcher stops an Implementer VM at 3600 seconds). A turn that is still running at the limit is cut. The cost of a turn is not set here: it is capped by what is left of `budgetUsd`.

onFailure.description: Steps that run once after the run ended `failed` or `cancelled`, never after `succeeded` (#902). The run keeps its final status. The form is that of `steps`; the validator holds them to comments (`ticket.comment`, `github.issue.comment`), label changes (`ticket.labels`, `github.issue.labels`) and `if` over them (`on_failure_step_not_allowed`), gives them `{{failure.status}}`, `{{failure.stepId}}`, `{{failure.code}}` and `{{failure.message}}` and none of the steps above, and counts them against the 50 steps of the document.

Template.description: A text; `{{step.field}}` in it is replaced by the value of that field when the step runs. `{{step.field | default <JSON>}}` gives a value for a field that may be missing. `\{{` is a literal `{{`.

Reference.description: A text that is exactly one reference and nothing else (no text and no space around it), where a number, true/false or a list is wanted: the value keeps its type. The `default` of a reference may hold braces nested three deep and JSON strings that hold `}}`. The pattern is `REFERENCE_PATTERN` of src/workflows/template.ts.

profile.description: A profile, `name` for the newest version or `name@version` to pin one.

environment.description: The name of an environment of the workspace, as a literal: it decides where the agent works, so version 1 takes no reference (`target_from_untrusted_value`, checked by the validator).

instruction.description: The task. A loop body may give `first` (round one) and `next` (later rounds, where `{{previous.<step>.<field>}}` is available).

session.description: `new` (default) or the session of an earlier agent step, or of this step itself in the round before.

branch.description: The branch a session of its own starts from, instead of the base branch of the run: a literal, `{{trigger.repo.defaultBranch}}`, an input of a manual trigger or `{{<agent step>.branch}}` (the branch of an earlier agent step that may push). A target, so no other reference (`target_from_untrusted_value`); not with `session.continue` (checked by the validator: a session that goes on keeps its branch).

result.description: What the agent's result looks like; the finish tool is made from it. Without one the step yields the facts only (and the result schema of the profile, once profiles bring one).

head.description: A branch: a literal, or exactly one reference to the branch of an agent step that may push (`{{implement.branch}}`). The validator refuses anything else.

base.description: A branch: a literal, or exactly one reference to `{{trigger.repo.defaultBranch}}` or to an input of a manual trigger (`{{trigger.input.<name>}}`). The default branch of the repository when left out. The validator refuses anything else.

IssueInput.description: A positive whole number up to 2147483647, or exactly one reference to the issue of the trigger (`{{trigger.issue}}`, `{{trigger.issue.number}}`, `{{trigger.ticket}}`, `{{trigger.ticket.number}}`) or to an input of a manual trigger that is declared `integer`. The default of a reference is held to the same rule. The validator refuses the title, body and labels of the issue, and the engine checks the number again when it runs.

LabelsInput.description: Label names: a list of literals and references to inputs of a manual trigger (`{{trigger.input.<name>}}`, one reference per entry), or exactly one reference to a list input. The title, body and labels of the issue, and an agent's result, are data and are not taken (`target_from_untrusted_value`). An action may not add the label that starts the workflow (`label_retriggers_workflow`).

maxRounds.description: At most this many rounds, 1 to 10. The loop ends earlier when `until` holds (exit `until`) or when the workflow budget is used up between two rounds (exit `budget`). Afterwards `{{<loop id>.exit}}` is `until`, `maxRounds` or `budget` and `{{<loop id>.rounds}}` the number of rounds that ran; the steps of the body keep the values of the last round.

ReservedStep.description: Reserved: `forEach`, `approval` and a workflow as a step are named so a document can use them in a later version. Version 1 refuses them (`kind_not_supported`); their other fields are not defined yet.

Operand.description: A reference like "{{review.findings}}", a text, a number or true/false.

Condition.description: Exactly one operator. `empty`/`notEmpty` ask whether a list or text is empty; `equals`/`notEquals` compare two texts, numbers or true/false values; `all`, `any`, `not` combine. Nested four levels deep at most (the validator).

ManualTriggerEntry.description: Started by hand (`manual`) or through the API (`api`; the start form offers `manual` only). `input` declares what the caller hands in; steps read it as `{{trigger.input.<field>}}`. A run works on one repository: the input declares either `ticket` (type `ticket`, required: a reference like `github:owner/repo#128`; the run works in the repository of the ticket and steps read it as `{{trigger.ticket.number|title|body|labels|type|assignees|url|repo|repo.defaultBranch}}`) or `repo`, a required text (owner/name). The schema cannot say it (`repo_required`).

TicketLabeledTriggerEntry.description: Started when the label is put on a ticket (an issue of a repository of the workspace). Steps read `{{trigger.ticket.number}}`, `.title`, `.body`, `.url`, `.labels`, `.type`, `.assignees`, `.repo` and, as workflows written before #916 do, `{{trigger.issue.number}}`, `.title`, `.body`, `.url`, `.labels` and `{{trigger.repo.fullName}}`, `.owner`, `.name`, `.defaultBranch`. `github.issueLabeled` is the old name of `ticket.labeled`.

label.description: The label that starts the workflow. Two `ticket.labeled` triggers of one workflow may not wait for the same label, in any case (`duplicate_trigger_label`: the schema cannot say it, the validator does).

PullRequestPushedTriggerEntry.description: Reserved (#916): a push to a pull request. The format validates it, the engine starts no run from it yet.

ScheduleTriggerEntry.description: Reserved (#916): a schedule, `cron` with five fields separated by one space. The format validates it, the engine starts no run from it yet.

ManualTrigger.description: Started by hand (`manual`) or through the API (`api`; the start form offers `manual` only). `input` declares what the caller hands in; steps read it as `{{trigger.input.<field>}}`. A run works on one repository: the input declares either `ticket` (type `ticket`, required: a reference like `github:owner/repo#128`; the run works in the repository of the ticket and steps read it as `{{trigger.ticket.number|title|body|labels|type|assignees|url|repo|repo.defaultBranch}}`) or `repo`, a required text (owner/name). The schema cannot say it (`repo_required`).

TicketLabeledTrigger.description: Started when the label is put on a ticket (an issue of a repository of the workspace). Steps read `{{trigger.ticket.number}}`, `.title`, `.body`, `.url`, `.labels`, `.type`, `.assignees`, `.repo` and, as workflows written before #916 do, `{{trigger.issue.number}}`, `.title`, `.body`, `.url`, `.labels` and `{{trigger.repo.fullName}}`, `.owner`, `.name`, `.defaultBranch`. `github.issueLabeled` is the old name of `ticket.labeled`.

PullRequestPushedTrigger.description: Reserved (#916): a push to a pull request. The format validates it, the engine starts no run from it yet.

ScheduleTrigger.description: Reserved (#916): a schedule, `cron` with five fields separated by one space. The format validates it, the engine starts no run from it yet.

Trigger.description: The single trigger of the older form: the same kinds, without `id` and `steps`.

TriggerEntry.description: One entry of `triggers`: the same kinds, each with an `id` (unique among the triggers, the start API names it) and `steps`, the pre-steps that run first when this trigger started the run.

TriggerSteps.description: The pre-steps of a trigger: the form of `steps`, and may be empty. They see only the values of their own trigger; the shared steps after them see only what every trigger yields.

TriggerInput.description: The input of a manual or api trigger: a result schema (result-schema.v1.json) whose fields may also be `ticket`, a reference to a ticket like `github:owner/repo#128`. Only a field of the input itself may be a ticket, and it is called `ticket`.

TicketTarget.description: As `IssueInput`, for the action on a ticket: a positive whole number up to 2147483647, or exactly one reference to the ticket of the trigger (`{{trigger.ticket}}`, `{{trigger.ticket.number}}`, or the issue of a label trigger, `{{trigger.issue}}`) or to an input of a manual trigger that is declared `integer`. A trigger that does not yield a ticket makes the reference `reference_not_in_scope`.
